papers.title: E2GNN: Efficient Graph Neural Network Ensembles for Semi-Supervised Classification
papers.operation: Independently pretrained GCN/GAT/APPNP/GraphSAGE/SGC teachers; MLP student; student-hidden-state MLP policy chooses one teacher or null per node; student CE plus selected-teacher KL; alternating policy-gradient and student updates. The policy gradient is trained using validation labels Eq5/6. Default alpha=0 makes student direct CE term zero while teacher fits and validation policy remain supervised.
papers.closest_role: Recent direct graph node-conditioned reliable-teacher/ensemble distillation ancestry; not dense served error-moment pooling. Equal-output ensemble and equal/adaptive multi-teacher distillation are explicit baselines.
limitations: No code/native reproduction, full paper, visual/result audit or empirical gain adopted.
Native validation-label policy training cannot be compared as a TRAIN-only meta-stage without matching supervision.
Text samples actions, while Eq1 prints argmax policy selection; operational resolution needs source.
Negative-KL reward Eq2 favors smaller teacher/student KL among correct teachers; the larger-amount-of-learning prose is not adopted as an algebraic conclusion.
Default MLP graph knowledge is inherited via teacher targets, not direct topology diffusion at serving.
papers.attribution_consequence: Reliable teacher selection on graph-derived states and student fusion are established. This method does not prove graph-local residual cross-moment estimation improves accuracy.

papers.title: A Collaborative Ensemble Framework for CTR Prediction
papers.operation: Separate InterFormer/DHEN embedding tables and dense feature MLPs; symmetric prediction KL collaboration; detached negative Bernoulli entropy gives softmax weights; weighted hidden-embedding concatenation and sigmoid readout; fusion BCE plus two member BCE plus alpha symmetric KL.
papers.closest_role: Recent concurrent collaboration and dense hidden-state fusion ancestry beyond GNNs. Exact weights are confidence-derived rather than labeled residual cross-moments.
limitations: CTR, two distinct model families and private embedding tables; no target GNN classification transfer.
Confidence can be high on incorrect predictions; entropy is not conditional competence or error covariance.
Consistency reduces prediction difference; it does not establish useful complementary errors.
No code/native reproduction, full paper, results, cost or publication qualification adopted.
papers.attribution_consequence: Concurrent branch competence losses, mutual consistency and representation fusion are component ancestry; do not present them as new multi-head ideas.

papers.title: Multi-Head Attention as Ensemble Nadaraya-Watson Estimation: Variance Reduction, Decorrelation, and Optimal Head Diversity
papers.operation: Models scalar attention heads as Nadaraya-Watson estimators and their output as a fixed positive simplex-weighted sum. Eq3.3 expands MSE into squared common-target bias, individual variances and pairwise covariances.
papers.closest_role: Recent explicit multi-head covariance discussion; restricted algebra corroborates ordinary weighted-ensemble ancestry, not a new covariance-weighting principle.
limitations: Setup uses scalar regression, iid samples, common target and positive weights summing to one.
General transformer output projection is not constrained to scalar simplex weights; transfer to standard MHA/GNNs is unqualified.
Kernel/NW consistency, principal-angle covariance bounds, monotonicity, optimal projection/architecture claims and geometric weights were not audited/adopted.
No classification accuracy/MRR guarantee, graph-correlated sampling guarantee, empirical result or code read.
papers.attribution_consequence: Use only the standard weighted-ensemble bias/variance/covariance identity under its stated aggregation; no attention geometry theorem supplies a graph-quality guarantee.

analyst_operator_identity: For multiclass Brier errors e_m=p_m-onehotY, e_m dot e_n=(||e_m||²+||e_n||²-||p_m-p_n||²)/2. Same-anchor graph averaging preserves the identity. Full off-diagonal moments are equivalent to local diagonal competence plus pairwise disagreement, not an independent labeled statistic; no duplicate experiment proposed.
